column1: # Every body in this directory, the diff it is read against, and the verdict
# Every expectation here was derived from GitHub's own renderer — each body was
# POSTed to `/markdown` and the verdict read off the HTML that came back: which
# headings exist, which images exist, what each one loads from. Not from what
# seemed reasonable, and not from what the check happened to say. Twice now a
# fixture has been the thing that was wrong rather than the code, and both times
# it was because somebody wrote down what they expected instead of asking.
# ---- honest bodies, which must keep passing --------------------------------
# These matter more than the attacks. A false failure costs a contributor; a
# missed bypass costs a review. The four heading forms below were all refused
# by the old hand-written parser and all four render as plain `<h2>`.
# The dark-mode `<picture>` idiom written honestly, both URLs on an allowed
# host. Refusing this would punish somebody for following GitHub's own docs.
# An allowed host named in a sentence, or sitting in the alt text of a
# fork-hosted ``. What counts is where the picture loads from.
# GitHub refuses this URL outright and renders ``, so there is no
# picture at all — which is why this says no-evidence and not not-hosted.
# A decoy attribute ahead of the real one. `data-src` was read instead of
# `src`; `srcset` carries the allowlisted decoy while `src` carries the fork,
# and GitHub strips `srcset` from an `` — so the fork is what renders.
# The same idea one layer in: `src=` written inside an *earlier attribute's
# value*. GitHub keeps author attribute order and keeps single quotes inside a
# double-quoted value, so `alt="x src='<allowed>'"` sat ahead of the real
# `src` and a regex searching the tag found the decoy first. The attributes
# are walked as name=value pairs now, so a value can only be a value. The `>`
# one is here because a `>` in an alt comes back as `>` — which is what
# lets the tag end where it looks like it ends.
# A `` shows its first matching `` and keeps the `` only
# as a fallback, and GitHub preserves `<source srcset>` un-proxied. The `media`
# spelling shows the fork to every reviewer in dark mode and to nobody else.
# Raw HTML opened on the line straight after a paragraph: GitHub stops reading
# markdown there, so every `##` under it comes out as literal text. Both of
# these used to be counted as headings anyway. The first is the same body as
# picture-source-shadow with `media` on it, and it loses two of its four.
